title: Comparing DWV Piping: ABS vs. PVC
description: Choosing between Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) is essential when installing DWV drainage systems. ABS is a rigid black pipe joined using a single-step solvent cement, making joint assembly faster in low-temperature environments. PVC is a white plastic pipe that requires a two-step process using purple primer to soften the pipe surfaces before applying cement for a true chemical weld. While both materials handle residential wastewater effectively, PVC offers higher impact strength and better sound attenuation, whereas ABS offers superior cold-weather flexibility. Always verify local plumbing codes, as mixing pipe materials requires specific transition fittings.

PVC is a white plastic pipe that requires a two-step process using purple primer to soften the pipe surfaces before applying cement for a true chemical weld. While both materials handle residential wastewater effectively, PVC offers higher impact strength and better sound attenuation, whereas ABS offers superior cold-weather flexibility. Always verify local plumbing codes, as mixing pipe materials requires specific transition fittings.
